## Content enrichment candidate — 2026.10.1-rc.3

The candidate contains ten volumes, 71 chapters and 406 canonical documents. The first enrichment introduced object-storage and network chapters plus twelve deeper mechanism treatments. This second pass adds five distinct mechanism pages and three complete original worked designs within existing chapters. Counts describe membership, not acceptance.

The rc.3 baseline contains 406 canonical documents. The #227 P2 delivery adds
one canonical page, the V04/C05 periodic-work page, after that baseline, for a
current canonical corpus of 407. The historical 406 count remains the rc.3
membership.

| New mechanism | Worked integration |
| --- | --- |
| [Configuration rollout](volumes/v08-delivery-deployment-and-recovery/c04-gitops-rollout-and-progressive-delivery/configuration-rollout.md) and [cells/shuffle sharding](volumes/v08-delivery-deployment-and-recovery/c06-high-availability-and-failure-domain-placement/cells-shuffle-sharding.md) | [A multitenant service under overload](volumes/v10-decision-support-and-modernization/c07-cross-domain-worked-comparisons-and-unresolved-cases/multitenant-project.md) |
| [Session observations](volumes/v04-distributed-coordination-and-events/c02-replication-consensus-and-leader-changes/session-consistency.md) and [offline conflicts](volumes/v04-distributed-coordination-and-events/c03-consistency-and-distributed-transactions/multiwriter-conflicts.md) | [Offline collaboration](volumes/v10-decision-support-and-modernization/c07-cross-domain-worked-comparisons-and-unresolved-cases/collaboration-project.md) |
| [Protocol correctness verification](volumes/v01-requirements-and-architecture/c04-evidence-hypotheses-and-architecture-experiments/protocol-correctness.md) | [A large-file catalogue](volumes/v10-decision-support-and-modernization/c07-cross-domain-worked-comparisons-and-unresolved-cases/catalogue-project.md) |

Every project states its synthetic workload, authority, normal/failure/recovery paths, alternatives, cost arithmetic and conditions that reverse the choice. Source versions, actual read scopes and unknowns remain explicit. See the [second-pass contract](../authoring/SECOND_ENRICHMENT_CONTRACT_2026-10-20.md) and [validation record](../authoring/SECOND_ENRICHMENT_VALIDATION_2026-10-20.md).

The execution environment is available again: 16/16 Python groups, 233/233 tests with zero skips, and 221/221 Mermaid syntax parses passed. Python reproduced the candidate index byte for byte. See [executed validation](../authoring/PYTHON_MERMAID_VALIDATION_2026-10-20.md). #214 remains open for substantive acceptance.

tasks.heading: Contrasting historical evidence
tasks.title: Decision Playbook — Reactive event loops, virtual threads and queued I/O
tasks.content:
## Contrasting historical evidence

| Case or mechanism | What its source does and does not establish |
|---|---|
| [Netflix gateway](../netflix-zuul2-nonblocking-gateway.md) | src.m9-n07: Zuul2 gained connection scale; CPU gain differed by cluster |
| [Java 21 pinning][pin] | JEP 444/491 mechanism; no incident counts |
| [Netflix gRPC worker pool](../netflix-grpc-cpu-workerpool-virtual-thread-regression.md) | src.m9-n02: 2023 practitioner account of a CPU-intensive outgoing gRPC worker pool that became a **few percent slower** after trying virtual threads; no exact benchmark published |
| [Cloudflare](../cloudflare-super-slurper-queues.md) | src.m9-cf01: I/O copy fan-out via queues/workers, small-test regression |

**Why the apparent conflict is useful:** Zuul2 exposes network connection scaling as a primary
win even without universal CPU gains; JDK 21 monitor pinning exposes a hidden synchronization
risk, while the separate CPU-intensive gRPC worker-pool experiment became slower without any
carrier-pinning incident; Cloudflare's queue fan-out addresses asynchronous tasks at a different
durability granularity.

tasks.heading: Engineering walkthrough — The cancel-versus-accept invariant crosses a transaction boundary
tasks.title: Consistency, transaction isolation and sagas across service boundaries
tasks.content:
## Engineering walkthrough — The cancel-versus-accept invariant crosses a transaction boundary

**Original fictional reservation:** Booking accepts one seat and Payment authorizes a deposit in separate databases. Cancellation can race with payment confirmation. Two transactions may each be locally ACID yet produce a globally invalid result: booking CANCELLED while the external payment is captured as if the booking remained ACTIVE.

A local PostgreSQL serializable transaction can protect a booking-state transition inside one data authority, subject to retries. It cannot atomically roll back a committed capture in an unrelated payment provider. A saga must define valid durable states and compensating actions, including cases where payment capture cannot be reversed instantaneously.

| Event race | Business protocol response | Incorrect shortcut |
|---|---|---|
| Cancel before payment authorized | Mark cancellation intent; prevent new capture through fenced operation/state | Assume last message received always wins |
| Payment captured, cancel then arrives | Transition to refund-pending and reconcile actual refund effect | Rewrite captured to never-happened |
| Deposit reply lost | Query provider by stable payment intent | Blindly capture a second payment |
| Compensation fails | Durable retry/manual repair state with accountable owner | Declare saga complete while money remains captured |

**Choice:** if all required state can remain in one local database, prefer its transaction/invariant over a saga for that operation; when independent business authorities are non-negotiable, accept explicit intermediate states and compensation contracts. A message order alone cannot substitute for versioned business transitions. The saga pattern and PostgreSQL isolation documents support bounded mechanisms, not guaranteed reversibility.

**Proposed, not executed:** synchronize cancel and accept operations, lose payment acknowledgments, crash during compensation and replay messages out of order. The test oracle is one legal booking outcome plus independently reconciled payment status, not a globally atomic transaction claim.

<!-- /tycho-question-source -->

tasks.heading: 1. Keep five distinct contracts
tasks.title: State authority and coexistence transitions
tasks.content:
## 1. Keep five distinct contracts

| Contract | Target state must say | Every transition state must additionally say |
|---|---|---|
| Functional ownership | Which capability accepts each user-visible operation | Whether old or new implementation receives each client/version |
| State authority | Where each authoritative entity is written and validated | How double-writing is prevented, which source is current, and how to reconcile |
| API/event semantics | Public operation identity, schema, ordering and errors | Old/new versions simultaneously supported, unknown outcomes and replay horizon |
| Security/operations | Trust boundaries, access control, dependency/service budget | Which principal/role may switch routing or write, and whose on-call can recover |
| Failure and recovery | Long-term RPO/RTO and availability model | Exact cutover rollback window, irreversible effects, restore and forward-repair path |

A target architecture might consist of one improved modular application; a transition need not split services. Conversely, a migration that introduces a second deployment needs extra protection even if the target only promises the same user journey.

<!-- /tycho-question-source -->

tasks.heading: 1. Separate replica types and required properties
tasks.title: Replica properties and quorum failure envelopes
tasks.content:
## 1. Separate replica types and required properties

| Mechanism | Can provide | What it does not automatically give |
|---|---|---|
| Independent read replica | More read capacity and recovery options | Strong current reads or no lag |
| Asynchronous replication | Durable-copy pipeline with bounded/observed lag under policy | Zero loss at primary failure |
| Leader-based consensus replication | Shared committed-log decisions while quorum and assumptions hold | Client progress without sufficient voters |
| Multi-writer replication | Concurrent writes in different locations | Globally serializable conflict-free outcomes |
| Historical backup and PITR | Recovery to a supported prior state if chain intact | Immediate failover or no acknowledged data loss |

For each architecture specify write acknowledgment, eligible reader, membership configuration, failure domain, consistency, reconfiguration and restore model. “Replicated” alone is not an acceptance criterion.

<!-- /tycho-question-source -->
